frameworks.name: comparative_advantage
frameworks.notes: France's RCA is extreme: CFM International (GE–Safran 50/50) makes the world's dominant narrow-body engines; Safran builds the low-pressure sections in Villaroche. Few countries can produce turbofans at all.

frameworks.name: gravity
frameworks.notes: Engine trade follows aircraft deliveries and MRO networks; gravity works via airline fleet size and GDP.

products.name: commercial_aircraft_engines
products.notes: Turbojets/turbofans (CFM LEAP, CFM56 via CFM International JV; Snecma/Safran share). Effectively a duopoly-with-GE product. JV structure complicates 'French product' claim — discuss in paper.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.notes: Fast-growing airline market (VietJet, Vietnam Airlines operate A320neo family with LEAP engines); expanding MRO sector; minimal existing French engine-services link.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.notes: Largest SE Asian aviation market; Lion Air 737 MAX fleet uses LEAP-1B; huge MRO gap.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.notes: Air Astana growing; French aerospace ties nascent; Air Astana signed for A320neo family.

trade_links.source: estimate — engines usually ship via JV entities, customs attribution may be US or France; verify attribution rule
